Now I am going to tell you what it was that K54 said that Colonel Delic on that same day when the action in Jeskovo was carried out was at the entrance to the village and he heard him say that then - he's from your logistics battalion - he heard him say then that they were going to clean the village from the KLA. Who's lying, him or you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: That's not correct at all. The entire class of march knows that, they were all there the previous day when he called us to talk to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, K82. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I do apologise, I think that I went on for another five minutes after the usual time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Just one matter. You said that the quotation from the Milosevic trial was an exhibit. It's not been presented as one of the Prosecution exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No, Your Honour. I think that yet again -- well, I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty. I don't want to make any false accusations, but I think that what I said was that since this is not an exhibit, I am asking him about it so that we in turn could quote the transcript saying what it was that he was asked. And one more thing, Your Honours, if I may ask you, 5D132 and 133, could they please be exhibits under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I think the last was my misunderstanding. K82, we require to break again and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Bakrac, my colleague, was very thorough and I have perhaps five or six questions only for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. K82. I would just like to put a few questions to you, and first and foremost in the Milosevic case you were shown P2062. I am not asking to tender this document. I am just trying to lay a foundation for my questions. That is the order of Colonel Delic from the 4th of February, 1999, in which it says in paragraph 12, and it is addressed to all units within the 549th Brigade. In that paragraph 12 it says: "Familiarise all units and personnel with the provisions of the Geneva Convention and the treatment of imprisoned and wounded members of the enemy force." Mr. K82, did that actually happen? Were you personally informed about the provisions of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as for actions that you took part in with your unit, you personally had no knowledge about intelligence data and assessments that had to do with certain localities and that were perhaps accessible to the commander of your brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge as to whether at that time Colonel or General Delic had information like that, intelligence like that, prior to these actions; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I really don't know how it is that I could have known about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, finally, a document that was exhibited by the Prosecution, and it's on their list that my colleague Mr. Stamp showed to you but it's a different provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly put document P1981 on e-court. Let me just find the page reference, please. 5.6 is the item that I'd like to see. In English it's page 4 and in B/C/S it's page 3. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out to you what it says here in 5.6. "Forces to seal off territory," and then it says: "Parts of Trnje, the Jezero feature and Mistra feature and so on are carried out by parts of the logistics battalion and other units and their task is to prevent the Siptar terrorist forces from withdrawing through their positions." In the order that is what it says and nowhere in this order issued by General Delic does it say that the villages should be attacked and torched and that no one should remain alive. Am I not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: As for what I know, I know what was going on in the field and as for these provisions I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I know what you said. This document was shown to you while you gave your last statement, and you spoke about that in paragraph 8 of your statement. You said that you read that order. I read it out to you again, now, and I'm asking you on the basis of what I read out to you, the order -- isn't it true that it doesn't say that the villages were supposed to be attacked and that no one should remain alive and that it was not the task of your logistics battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K82
utterances.text: I am repeating once again, no order was read in front of us except for what I told you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No questions witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: K82, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the office to give that evidence, and that brings the need for your presence there to an end. You're free to leave the office as soon as the videolink is disconnected, which should be now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What now, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next witness is K87, who I -- who we propose to put on tomorrow at 9.00. I don't think he's ready yet. He probably arrived today or late last night and he is not available for testimony today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall resume then tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
